newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Alliance Pipeline files NEB application.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Alliance Pipeline files NEB application.

text.p: Alliance Pipeline Ltd, which aims to build a C$3.6 billion natural gas pipeline to Chicago from northern Canada, said on Thursday it filed its application with Canada's National Energy Board.
Alliance, a joint venture of 18 energy companies, said it intended to start construction on the 3,000 km line in 1998 for startup in late 1999.
Thursday's move followed a similar filing late last year with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
Partners in Alliance, which would ship 1.3 billion cubic feet of gas per day, include such companies as Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Chauvco Resources Ltd and IPL Energy Inc.

The company reiterated that its purpose was to boost market access for western Canadian gas, now constrained by tight pipeline capacity, and to cut the price discount of Canadian gas compared to that in eastern North American Markets.

Alliance is in competition with several traditional pipeline firms, led by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, which have also proposed major expansions of pipe capacity to U.S. Midwest and northeast markets from western Canada.
The company said it was supported by long-term commitments from 35 gas shippers which contracted capacity totalling 1.294 billion cubic feet per day, about 98 percent of its total firm space.
Of those, 29 shippers are western Canadian exploration and production companies, which together pump out over a third of the region's gas, it said.

"The filing of this application with the National Energy Board represents a giant step towards our goal of providing shippers with a competitive transportation alternative for western Canadian gas production," Alliance Chief Executive Dennis Cornelson said in a statement.

Including the pipeline's U.S. portion, shippers committed to payments of C$8.2 billion for gas transport service on Alliance over the 15-year term of the agreements, the company said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
